value.body: Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry. You study animal anatomy, medicine, surgery and gynaecology alongside livestock, dairy and poultry production, then complete a one-year internship. It is regulated by the Veterinary Council of India (VCI).

items.note: All modes; a further ~5,400 are listed separately as B.V.Sc.

items.label: All India Quota seats
items.note: 15% of seats in recognised colleges, counselled by VCI

items.note: 56 fully recognised, the rest provisionally recognised
items.source: Rajya Sabha reply, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English, and a NEET-UG score. VCI counsels the 15% All India Quota online; states fill the remaining 85% through their own counselling, usually on NEET-UG scores.

value.title: At a glance
items: Practice needs registration with the VCI or a State Veterinary Council.
State animal husbandry departments run veterinary hospitals and recruit veterinary officers.
An M.V.Sc. (admission mostly via ICAR AIEEA-PG or state tests) is the usual way to specialise.
